correctness.rationale: The private-neighborhood converse is complete. A one-part set is independent and self-private. If an irredundant set meets multiple parts, a selected vertex needs an external private vertex; complete-multipartite adjacency forces every other selected vertex into that private vertex's part. Repeating from the opposite part forces exactly one selected vertex in each of two parts, and the external private vertices require both parts to have size at least two. Maximality and both enumerators then follow by disjoint counting. A fresh literal replay checked 10,668 subsets through total order seven; this finite replay is corroborative, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for a foundational graph parameter on a canonical graph class. It simultaneously determines every feasible set, every maximal feasible set, two standard enumerators, and both extremal irredundance numbers. The exact structural information is stronger than a scalar parameter computation and is plausibly reusable.

final_claim: For every connected complete multipartite graph \(K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\), the irredundant sets are exactly the empty set, subsets of one part, and two-vertex transversals between distinct non-singleton parts; consequently the stated irredundance and maximal-irredundance polynomials and the formulas for \(\operatorname{IR}(G)\) and \(\operatorname{ir}(G)\) hold.
limitations: Graphs must be connected complete multipartite with at least two nonempty parts.
